llm.reply:
Three genes are linked to Li-Fraumeni syndrome [2]. The first is NCBIGene:7157, tumor protein p53 [4]. The second is NCBIGene:11200, checkpoint kinase 2 [3]. The third is NCBIGene:1029, cyclin dependent kinase inhibitor 2A [1].

## TP53 as primary cause

The literature describes Li-Fraumeni syndrome as a dominantly inherited cancer predisposition caused by germline TP53 mutation [19: "a cancer predisposition syndrome caused by a germline mutation of the TP53 gene on chromosome 17p13.1"]. Loss of p53 function allows malignancies to develop across the lifespan [19: "TP53 gene mutations cause the loss of function of p53, leading to downstream events permissive for development of various malignancies throughout life"]. One case report identified a specific germline TP53 variant [21: "revealed the germinal mutation c.527G>T (p.Cys176Phe) on exon 5 of the TP53 gene"].

## Phenotypic heterogeneity

Carriers of the same pathogenic TP53 variant can show different phenotypes [22: "Phenotypic heterogeneity is present among different families affected by the same pathogenic variant in TP53 gene"]. Proposed modifiers include polymorphisms and copy number changes [22: "polymorphic variants in TP53 gene or in TP53-related genes, copy number variations in particular regions"].

## Clinical research

Registered studies include Clinical and Genetic Studies of Li-Fraumeni Syndrome [17]. Another study is LIFSCREEN : Evaluation of Whole Body MRI for Early Detection of Cancers in Subjects With P53 Mutation (Li-Fraumeni Syndrome) [20].

The graph links three genes to Li-Fraumeni syndrome. The first is NCBIGene:1029, cyclin dependent kinase inhibitor 2A [1]. The second is NCBIGene:11200, checkpoint kinase 2 [3]. The third is NCBIGene:7157, tumor protein p53 [4]. The disease record is named Li-Fraumeni syndrome [2].

## TP53 as cause

Reviews describe the syndrome as a dominantly inherited cancer predisposition caused by germline TP53 mutation [19: "caused by a germline mutation of the TP53 gene on chromosome 17p13.1"][19: "autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance with high penetrance"]. Loss of p53 function allows tumours such as sarcomas, breast cancer, brain tumours and adrenocortical carcinomas to develop [19: "TP53 gene mutations cause the loss of function of p53"][19: "soft tissue sarcomas, osteosarcoma, premenopausal breast cancer, brain tumors, and adrenal cortical carcinomas"]. One Colombian case report found a pathogenic germline TP53 variant [21: "revealed the germinal mutation c.527GT (p.Cys176Phe) on exon 5 of the TP53 gene"].

## Phenotypic heterogeneity

Families carrying the same TP53 variant can still show very different phenotypes [22: "Phenotypic heterogeneity is present among different families affected by the same pathogenic variant in TP53 gene"]. Possible modifiers include polymorphisms in TP53 or related genes and copy number changes [22: "polymorphic variants in TP53 gene or in TP53-related genes, copy number variations in particular regions"].

## Literature and trials

One indexed article is titled Li-Fraumeni Syndrome. [5]. A second is also titled Li-Fraumeni Syndrome. [13]. A third is titled Li-Fraumeni syndrome. [10]. A fourth is titled Li-Fraumeni syndrome heterogeneity. [16].

The MedGen concept is titled Li-Fraumeni syndrome [6]. The literature entity is named Li-Fraumeni Syndrome [7].

The related publications are PMID 27617148 [9], PMID 27622479 [12], PMID 30333936 [15] and PMID 31691207 [18].

Related clinical trials include:

- LIFSCREEN : Evaluation of Whole Body MRI for Early Detection of Cancers in Subjects With P53 Mutation (Li-Fraumeni Syndrome) [20].
